prs.title: Give each PROTEUS install its own Julia depot
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description Follows and Continues to create fully isolated PROTEUS environments per install so two installs do not interfere with each other. Two PROTEUS installs on one machine shared their Julia packages and compile files in `~/.julia`, so a package change in one reached the other. With this PR, `install.sh` keeps them in `$CONDA_PREFIX/julia_depot` and sets `JULIA_DEPOT_PATH` to that folder with a trailing colon, which keeps the compile files that come with Julia and does not add `~/.julia`. The Julia binary stays with juliaup, because conda-forge has no Julia for Apple Silicon. No result of a run should change, and no physics file changes. - A `JULIA_DEPOT_PATH` that is already set stays, with 2 exceptions: a `julia_depot` of another PROTEUS install is replaced, and so is one whose folder is gone from an `envs` folder. A value that is relative, names another user's home folder or holds a literal `$` stops the installer before it creates anything, and the message names the way out. - A value of your own now gives a warning. `bash install.sh -i` in a terminal asks `Use a Julia depot of its own for this install?` (default no), and `--ignore-julia-depot-path` keeps the value with one info line and no warning, except the depot of another install or of a gone environment. The installer never edits a shell start file and asks nothing without `-i` or a terminal, so CI and clusters see no question. - The installer and the doctor read the Julia manifest of a project by the 4 nam

prs.title: Couple the Aragog sub-grid lid to the atmosphere surface
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description A crust that forms at the surface of a magma ocean starts metres thick or less, while the top cell of the Aragog mesh is kilometres thick. Aragog models such a crust as a sub-grid lid (FormingWorlds/aragog#100, with the surface of an atmosphere from FormingWorlds/aragog#108; released in fwl-aragog 26.11.8). This PR couples that lid to the surface balance of PROTEUS. It is off by default. With `interior_energetics.aragog.lid_mush_base = true`: - PROTEUS runs the Aragog lid with its base at the solidus. The lid needs the Aragog solid rheology, which this PR exposes as `interior_energetics.aragog.rheology.enabled` (default false). - The atmosphere call (AGNI or the dummy) sees the lid and the open surface as two conductors in parallel at one surface temperature. `lid_boundary` in `atmos_clim/common.py` writes this sum as one skin, so neither atmosphere module changes its surface balance. - Aragog holds the lid surface at the `T_surf` of the last atmosphere call. Where the lid would then conduct more than the atmosphere took from the lid part, the lid surface warms and loses that flux plus the slope of `F_atm` times the warming. The slope comes from the last 2 rows. With the dummy, the step runs once more with the secant slope across the step when it differs; AGNI keeps the row slope. - Under a lid, `F_int` is the mean surface flux of the step from the Aragog energy integral, so the energy the lid stores or releases is booked. - Each interior snapshot stores the li

prs.title: Derive the surface skin from saturated condensates, correct SLURM parameters, and correct plot_structure
prs.author: nichollsh
prs.body: ## Description Adds the option `atmos_clim.surface_d = surface_k = 'saturation'`. The conductive skin between the magma and the atmosphere then comes from the condensates that atmodeller saturates at the surface, such as graphite. How the skin is built: - Each saturated condensate is spread over 4 pi R_int^2 at its density as a layer. - The layers stack in series: d = sum(d_i) and k = d / sum(d_i / k_i). - While the stack has a thermal resistance d / k below 1e-5 m2 K W-1, the atmosphere module solves with the fixed surface state (T_surf = T_magma). Once a layer forms, it solves with the skin. - AGNI, JANUS and the dummy atmosphere receive the surface state and the skin of each iteration. Plots: - `plot_structure` joins the top of each interior profile to the base of its atmosphere profile. The segment is dashed where a conductive skin exists, and the legend then lists it. - Profile plots of SPIDER runs are now sampled to the end of the run. Before, the times had to match the snapshot names exactly. SPIDER names its JSON snapshots by the rounded year while the atmosphere keeps the sub-year time, so only the first whole-year iterations were plotted. On a 3e5 yr run this left 1, 31 and 61 yr; it now gives 8.7e3 to 3e5 yr. - The `plot_structure` entry point selects its times the same way as the run does. Before, a missing SPIDER snapshot could shift every later interior profile, and a run shorter than 1e3 yr was reduced to its last snapshot. The branch also carries the Mercury c

prs.title: Deprecate the duplicate density keys of the dummy and boundary interiors
prs.author: nichollsh
prs.body: ## Description The config set the mantle density in three keys that could disagree, for example across a grid: `interior_energetics.const_rho` (4000 kg/m3), `interior_energetics.dummy.mantle_rho` (4550 kg/m3) and `interior_energetics.boundary.silicate_density` (4103 kg/m3). The boundary interior also had its own `core_density` (10738 kg/m3) next to `interior_struct.core_density`. Closes #909. Changes: - The dummy interior reports its mantle mass over the mantle shell volume as its density, as the boundary interior already does. Before, it reported `dummy.mantle_rho` while it took its mantle mass from the structure, so the two disagreed. - `const_rho` stays the density of constant-properties mode: SPIDER and Aragog read it only when `const_properties = true`. The dummy interior also reads it for its fallback mantle mass when the helpfile row has no `M_int` or `M_core`, which a coupled run always provides. - The boundary interior read `silicate_density` only when `interior_struct.module == 'self'`, the v2 name of the SPIDER structure, which no v3 validator accepts. It read `core_density` only when the helpfile row had no `R_core`, which every row has. Both branches are removed. The module takes `M_int`, `M_core` and `R_core` from the structure, raises `ValueError` when `M_int` is not above `M_core`, and raises `KeyError` when `M_int` is missing. The module map allowlist entry for the `'self'` comparison goes with the branch. - The SPIDER structure solves for the interior radius

prs.title: Stop install.sh from installing Julia
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description Part of #721. `install.sh` no longer installs Julia or adds a juliaup channel. It uses a Julia 1.13 that it finds, in this order: `PYTHON_JULIAPKG_EXE`, the `julia` on `PATH`, the `1.13` channel of juliaup, also when that juliaup is in `~/.juliaup/bin` beside a `julia` of another version. With no Julia 1.13 it stops with the commands to run, before `conda create`. Your default Julia stays as it is. A `julia` that is a juliaup launcher with no default channel counts as no Julia, because that launcher can install itself. The script asks juliaup only through `juliaup api getconfig1`, which downloads nothing on juliaup 1.23.0. A juliaup depot that you cannot write to counts as no Julia, because juliaup needs its lock file there. The stop quotes the error of juliaup and names `PYTHON_JULIAPKG_EXE`. The install page has a new step 2 for Julia. The Kapteyn and Cambridge IoA guides set `JULIAUP_DEPOT_PATH` before the official installer, so that the download does not land in a small home folder. Limits: - With a juliaup on your own `PATH`, the OpenSSL fall-back can still move PROTEUS to its 1.11 channel when that channel exists. `main` does the same. - A channel that juliaup lists while its files are gone can make the launcher download. I did not run this case. - A manual install without `install.sh` can still start a Julia download through juliacall (juliapkg `install_julia`). I leave this and the isolated-install design for #721, so this PR does not close it. Added li

prs.title: Let the sub-grid lid sit under the surface of an atmosphere
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description This lets the sub-grid crust (lid) act under a coupled atmosphere: with `outer_boundary_condition = 4` and the new switch `lid_mush_base`, the lid base sits at the solidus and the lid surface takes the temperature that the atmosphere holds through a call. A thin crust under a held flux would otherwise grow far past its steady thickness in one coupling step and melt back in the next. - `lid_mush_base`: the crust base at the solidus, with the eddy-diffusivity floor (`kappah_floor`) as the flux through the fluid part of the top cell, weighted to 0 at the solidus. - `lid_surface_temperature`, `lid_surface_flux_cap`, `lid_surface_flux_slope`: the held surface, the flux the last atmosphere balance gave the lid, and its slope with the surface temperature. Where the held lid would conduct more than the cap, the surface warms until it carries `C + F' (T_s - T_held)` (a Robin condition), in a form without overflow for large slopes, on NumPy and JAX. - For a base flux above 0, the lid weight rises without a step from the steady crust under the held surface (a tanh in the log of the steady thickness over `lid_delta_on`). - Start rules: a lid start with a value that is not finite is refused. With the mush base, a live lid over a top cell below the floor, or in the band where the heat jump of the base is below `LID_DH_MIN`, is refused in either order of `set_initial_lid` and `set_initial_entropy`; a set or carried lid at or above 0.7 of the top-cell width hands over at the s

prs.title: Book the core heat of a call from its integrated temperature change
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description With `core_bc = "core_module"`, Aragog keeps a per-call core energy ledger: the heat the core loses in a call (`step_dE_core_J`) must equal the heat that crosses the core-mantle boundary (CMB) in that call. The ledger booked the core heat change as the difference of the absolute heat contents at the start and the end of the call. An absolute core temperature near 5000 K holds a change only to its float spacing, about 9e-13 K. Times the effective heat capacity of the core, that is about 1e14 to 8e15 J per call. For a call with a small CMB heat this is a large part of it, so the ledger of such a call could not close. This PR books the core heat change from the change of the core temperature that CVODE integrates within the call: 1. Unstratified core: `CoreEnergyBudget.heat_change` in closed form, each side of freeze-out with its own capacity. 2. Stratified core (`stratification = true`): the trapezoid of the effective capacity over that change, plus the shell heat from the new `CoreShell.heat_change`. 3. New output `step_core_tol_J`: a diagnostic scale of the error of `step_dE_core_J` that the error control of the core temperature allows. It is NaN for every `core_bc` except `core_module`. 4. An `atol` below 1e-8 is raised to 1e-8 for the core temperature, with one log line. The change of the core temperature starts at 0, and CVODE needs a positive weight for it. The state that CVODE integrates and the right-hand side do not change. So the core and the mantle evo

prs.title: Add the liquidus of an iron core alloy with S, C and O
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description This PR adds `aragog.core.AlloyLiquidus`: the liquidus of a core made of iron with S, C, O, Si, H and N. S, C and O lower the melting point; Si, H and N are treated as lowering it not at all. The inner-core boundary lies where the core adiabat meets the liquidus. Where the liquidus is shallower than the adiabat, iron freezes first at the top of the core instead of at the centre. How the liquidus is built: 1. Each Fe-X binary is the ideal-solution form of Mori et al. (2017) and Mashino et al. (2019). It runs from pure iron (the Anzellini et al. 2013 curve) to the eutectic point. Fe is counted against FeS or Fe3S units for S, FeO for O, and Fe3C or Fe7C3 for C. 2. Several elements combine by a harmonic mean of the binary constants. 3. The eutectic points come from the Simon fits and figure curves of Mori et al. (2017), Mashino et al. (2019) and Oka et al. (2019), each figure read twice. Below 21 GPa the Fe-S eutectic comes from the nodes of Fei et al. (1997). The data run from 1 bar to 330 GPa (325 GPa for O). 4. A composition past its eutectic is held at the eutectic boundary. `AlloyLiquidus.status` flags it, and it flags every pressure above the data. The schematic at the top of the Explanation page: the liquidus of pure iron, 2 and 4.8 wt% S and the Fe-S eutectic against pressure, with an example core adiabat. All curves are computed from `AlloyLiquidus` when the figure is built (`tools/verification/figures/sketch_alloy_liquidus.py`). `AlloyLiquidus` is used t

prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description The sub-grid lid ran only under a grey-body surface with the EOS tables. This PR lets it run in 2 more setups, and uses them to check the lid on the stagnant-lid benchmarks and through a hand-over to the mesh. Code, all with `subgrid_lid = true` (the option stays off by default, and PROTEUS has no lid setting yet): - Outer boundary 5: the lid surface is held at the fixed surface temperature, and the shape of the lid follows from its energy at that temperature. - Constant-property column: the lid uses closed forms instead of the tables. It runs in one mode only: `entropy_eos=None`, the solid rheology with the `'lid'` closure, and `core_bc = 'quasi_steady'`. Other combinations stop at setup with an error. - Both run on the NumPy right-hand side only. `jax_lid_params()` refuses them by name. - `set_initial_entropy` now reads the current surface temperature, so a value set before that call reaches the start of the lid. A value set after it still does not change the start energy of the lid. Outputs that change: none in the 3 grey-body cases compared below, with and without the lid. Both new setups stopped at setup before this change. Config: `subgrid_lid` now also accepts outer boundary 5, and `const_properties` in the one mode above. No new keys. Breaking changes: none. Check 1, the benchmarks. A lid models a crust thinner than the top cell, so once it has handed over, a run must reach the steady state of the same run without the lid. The 12 rows with n = 1 of Kore

prs.title: Add a sub-grid conductive lid for a crust thinner than the top cell
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description A magma ocean need not freeze from its surface. The adiabat is steeper than the solidus, so the two meet first at depth and solidification is expected to begin at the bottom, the more so the larger the pressure range of the planet. An insulating atmosphere can keep the surface above its solidus for much of the solidification, and a quench crust on a planet-sized body is then unlikely (Elkins-Tanton 2012, Annu. Rev. Earth Planet. Sci. 40:113, section 4.1, A crust can still form at the surface when the surface loses heat faster than the melt below delivers it, for example under a thin atmosphere. Such a crust starts metres thick, while the top cell of a 100-node mantle is tens of kilometres thick. That cell has one temperature, so it is either all melt or all solid, and the surface flux is wrong in both states until a mesh resolves the crust. This PR adds an option, `subgrid_lid`, off by default. With it on, Aragog carries the crust as two extra states: its thickness and its energy per area. The temperature across the crust follows the textbook profile of a freezing layer. New crust forms at the base from the balance of the heat conducted up through the crust and the heat the melt delivers. The lid hands over to the mesh when the mesh can carry the crust. The NumPy and JAX paths both have it. New settings in `boundary_conditions`, explained in `docs/How-to/configuration.md`: | Setting | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `subgrid_lid` | false | Turns the lid on.

prs.title: Split bulk H, C, N and S between core and mantle with partition laws
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description This adds `calliope.core_split.split_core_mantle`, which splits the bulk H, C, N and S of a planet between the metal of the core and the silicate of the mantle at one equilibration point (default 60 GPa, 4000 K), with metal-silicate partition laws from the literature. PROTEUS does not call it yet; the coupling comes in a later PR. - Partition-law registry in `calliope.metal`: packaged laws for S (Suer et al. 2017 Eq. 7, with $X_\mathrm{FeO}$ from $\Delta\mathrm{IW}$ and the Fe of the metal), C (Fischer et al. 2020), H (Tagawa et al. 2021) and N (Suer et al. 2023), in `data/partition_laws_core.toml`; `register_law` adds a user law by name, as a file entry or a function. Each law carries its P, T and $\Delta\mathrm{IW}$ range; outside it the law is still used, and the split reports the distance to the range per element. - `split_core_mantle(bulk_kg, M_metal, M_silicate, *, dIW, ...)` returns `(core_kg, mantle_kg, flags)`. D depends on the metal composition, so the split is a fixed point on the metal mass fractions and the melt H and C. Plain passes first; where the metal takes so much S that the passes swing, relaxed passes with a per-element step factor, an iron floor of $10^{-8}$ by mass, and an acceptance on the float grid for very steep maps. Every split checks the element ledger (bulk = core + mantle, both $\geq 0$, to $10^{-12}$) and raises `RuntimeError` when it fails. - When a relaxed split ends on a metal with more S than Fe in moles, damped passes from

prs.title: Stop InsertStellarSpectrum hanging on a long output path
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description `InsertStellarSpectrum` no longer hangs and fills the disk on a long output path. Closes #79. `prep_spec` keeps a file name in 132 characters. A longer path was cut, the tool then asked for input it could not read, and it looped. It now runs in a temporary folder inside the output folder, with relative names and a `radiation_code.lock`, so the 132 characters no longer apply and a bad answer ends the program. What changes for a caller: - A folder above 190 bytes with its trailing separator stops with a `ValueError` before any file changes. The 190 comes from `MCICA_DATA` (`LEN=200`) in `l_run_cdf.F90` minus `mcica_data`. - A star file with no data marker, or a missing one, stops with a `ValueError`. `prep_spec` loops on such a file even with the lock. - A nonzero return code, a missing block 2 or 6 in `star.sf`, or a run past 1800 s stops with a `RuntimeError` that holds the last lines of the stderr of `prep_spec`. On main a nonzero return code gave only a warning, and a missing block gave nothing. These stops abort a PROTEUS run at start, as the issue asks. - Without the binary the error names `RAD_DIR`. A case that this makes visible: a star that ends exactly on an inner band edge. With a star ending at 1.0e-4 m on Oak 318, `prep_spec` exits with 0 and writes no block 2. Main goes on with no star in the file and no message. This branch stops with `*** error: wavelengths are incorrectly ordered.` A star ending at 1.01e-4 m passes. None of the 7 stored stars tha

prs.title: Add an escape regime dispatcher with per-species fractionation
prs.author: maraattia
prs.body: ## Summary - Adds `zephyrus.dispatch`: one planetary state in, one regime label, the branch that produced the rate, one bulk mass-loss rate, per-species rates summing to it, flags, and a boxed diagnostics container out. - Six labels: `boiloff`, `hydrodynamic:EL`, `hydrodynamic:RR`, `hydrodynamic:PL`, `hydrostatic`, `roche_overflow`, decided in a fixed order with every criterion's physical band reported beside the verdict. - Confirmed winds are split over species by an N-species fractionation closure. The released `EL_escape` keeps its import path and behavior apart from one tidal convention fix. - Standalone API for now: PROTEUS wiring (config schema, wrapper, profile transport) follows in a separate PR. ## Description This PR adds an escape regime dispatcher to ZEPHYRUS. One call, `zephyrus.dispatch`, takes a planetary state (scalars plus an atmosphere profile) and returns one regime label, the branch that produced the rate (`rate_branch`, which a time-stepping caller feeds back for the hysteresis window of the collisionality switch), one bulk mass-loss rate, per-species rates that sum to it, flags, and a boxed diagnostics container. Every physically posed input returns one and only one labeled result, and exceptions are reserved for malformed input. Every state receives one of six regime labels, decided in a fixed evaluation order: 1. Bolometrically driven boil-off: the Owen & Wu (2016) transonic Parker wind in exact Lambert-W form at the wind temperature T_eq/2^(1/4) of Mi

prs.title: Write every file of a standalone run into one output folder
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description `python -m zalmoxis` now writes all its files into one output folder: the profiles, the summary, the plots, `zalmoxis.log` and, at the DEBUG level, the 2 iteration profile files. The folder is the new `[Output]` key `output_dir` (an existing, writable folder), or else `output/` of the Zalmoxis root, which the run creates on a fresh checkout. Without `debug_profile_dir`, the command-line run puts the DEBUG dump into the same folder; a library or PROTEUS caller that sets neither key writes no file, as with - `load_zalmoxis_config` and `validate_config` refuse an `output_dir` that is not a string or path, is empty, or is not an existing, writable folder. - `plot_PT_with_phases` adds the mass to its file name (`mantle_PT_profile .pdf`), so a batch run no longer overwrites one file per mass. - The CLI log is a file handler in write mode at INFO; if the file cannot be opened, the log goes to stderr with a warning that names the file. - The grid runner `tools/grids/run_grid.py` does not use `output_dir`; usage.md says where it writes and which files stay outside the output folder (the EOS caches under `data/`). - Docs: configuration, usage, first run and installation pages; citations on the edited pages use footnotes. The branch merges main after #128 (merge commit d1ff740); the conflicts were in input/default.toml, config.py, `__main__.py`, AGENTS.md, configuration.md, usage.md and test_main_cli.py. The main test that mocked `logging.basicConfig` for the log path is

prs.title: Write the DEBUG profile dump only into a folder the caller names
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description A solve at the `DEBUG` log level wrote `pressure_profiles.txt` and `density_profiles.txt` into `output/` of the Zalmoxis source tree. Since #120 names the loggers under `fwl`, this also happens for a library or PROTEUS caller that turns on `DEBUG` for its own reasons. This PR makes the dump opt-in. - New key `debug_profile_dir` in `[Output]` (or in the config dict passed to `solver.main()`): an existing folder for the dump. Without it, a `DEBUG` solve logs as before and writes no file. - `load_zalmoxis_config` and `validate_config` refuse a wrong type, an empty string or `Path('')`, and a folder that does not exist. - The command-line run (`python -m zalmoxis`) sets the key to ` /output`, so the standalone behaviour stays the same. - `create_pressure_density_files` takes the folder as an argument. The files start again at the first pressure solve of each structure solve; usage.md now says that, instead of "at the start of each new run". - The surface pressure tutorial removes its temporary dump folder after reading it. PROTEUS builds its own config dict and sets no `debug_profile_dir`, so a coupled run writes no dump. No related issue. ## Validation of changes - `pytest tests/test_debug_profile_output.py tests/test_config_validators_extra.py tests/test_main_cli.py tests/test_eos_functions.py tests/test_accepted_on.py` on the branch source at 7a6a81f (macOS arm64, Python 3.12): 182 passed, 68 skipped. prs.title: Calibrate the core alloy density on the Hirose 2021 outer cores
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description The linear light-element law of the core alloy now puts each single-element outer core of Hirose et al. (2021, p. 3) 7 % below iron at the midpoint of its range: 13.3-14.4 wt% S, 9.3-9.8 wt% Si, 8.4-8.9 wt% O or 0.96-0.99 wt% H, each of which fits the seismic outer core 6 to 8 % below pure liquid iron. C and N keep the Li et al. (2019) values and are flagged as not calibrated. | Element | Old beta [% per wt%] | New beta [% per wt%] | |---|---|---| | S | 0.8 | 0.505 (7/13.85) | | Si | 0.7 | 0.733 (7/9.55) | | O | 1.1 | 0.809 (7/8.65) | | H | 8.7 (`CoreAlloy:H-linear`) | 7.18 (7/0.975, `CoreAlloy:H`) | The names of the 2 H laws change: - `CoreAlloy:H` is now the calibrated linear H law above. - The Fe-H2O carrier law of Luo et al. (2024), which `CoreAlloy:H` meant before, is now `CoreAlloy:H-Luo`. It removes the carrier O with the linear O law, so its effective beta_H moves from 12.83 to 15.14 % per wt% with the new beta_O (136 GPa, 8000 K). - `CoreAlloy:H-linear` is refused with an error that names both. No config in Zalmoxis (`input/`, `tools/`) or in PROTEUS main uses a `CoreAlloy` string (`git grep CoreAlloy`), and no Zalmoxis release contains `CoreAlloy` yet, so the new meaning of `CoreAlloy:H` changes no released config. I also added a warning when S, O and C together need more Fe than the core holds in the compound units of the alloy liquidus (Fe3S, FeO, Fe3C, Fe7C3). Density deficit against the PALEOS iron table at the low and high end of each Hirose rang

prs.title: Name the loggers under fwl so PROTEUS captures Zalmoxis logs
prs.author: stuitje
prs.body: ## Description Every module named its logger with `__name__`, which put it under a `zalmoxis` root. PROTEUS attaches its handlers to the `fwl` logger, so nothing Zalmoxis logged reached the PROTEUS logfile (#81). Only warnings and errors reached the terminal, without PROTEUS formatting. In this PR this is fixed: - All module loggers are now named `'fwl.' + __name__`. This follows the convention from FormingWorlds/fwl-io#34, commit f35f4d0. - The tests and the docs that name a Zalmoxis logger use the `fwl.zalmoxis.*` names. - The two benchmark scripts now quieten `fwl.zalmoxis.eos` and `fwl.zalmoxis.solver` (Issue #81, additional notes). The second replaces `zalmoxis.zalmoxis`, the solver module before #59. - When the INFO lines actually reached PROTEUS, the per-iteration ones spammed its log. They are now at DEBUG: the entropy-adiabat lines, `Newton iter N` and the log that the density iteration stopped early because of a lack of progress. - `Starting structure model`, `activating adiabat blend` and `Outer loop converged` are still at INFO for a standalone or a Picard solve. In a Newton solve, each M(R) probe logs them at DEBUG via a `_newton_probe` config flag. `Newton outer` and `Newton converged` show the start and end of the solve at INFO. - Warnings are unchanged. Closes #81. ## Validation of changes Zalmoxis tests pass. I ran: - Standalone `input/default.toml` converges in 173 s, with the same results as before the change. Its log has the three progress lines once each.

prs.title: Scale the reaction iterate to the time step after a cut
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview The outer thermomechanical iteration runs the hydration reaction at the start of each iteration and then the Stokes-Darcy solve, which can cut the time step. From the second iteration on, the reaction under-relaxes its new wet silicate fraction against the iterate of the previous iteration. After a cut that iterate held the progress of the longer step, and the mass transfer rate divided it by the shorter one. In `hydrothermal_reaction_on_32` the step is cut from 1e11 s to 2.47e5 s in step 33, and the accepted reaction progress of that step was about 1e5 times the progress of the next step at a similar time step. This PR scales the previous iterate to the current time step before the under-relaxation. The scale follows the reaction kinetics, so a scaled iterate equals the value a fresh call at the shorter step returns. ## Changes - Reaction (`src/physics/serpentinization.jl`): new keyword `dt_prev` (default `Δt`, no scaling). For `titer > 1` the log-odds `ln(XD/XW)` of the previous iterate, relative to the start value, are scaled by `min(Δt, t_c) / min(dt_prev, t_c)`, then clamped like the other iterates. `t_c` is the time at which the clamped path stops: `Δtr`, or earlier when the pore-water ceiling stops the reaction. The scaling is skipped for a pathway that is off, an iterate at the start value and a step without a cut. `Δt` and `dt_prev` must be positive and finite. `Δtr` has a default for a pathway that is off. - Outer loop (`src/simulation/steps/solve_thermo

prs.title: Give the pore fluid its own displacement limit and bound the fluid heat step
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview The adaptive time step limits the displacement per step to `dxymax` grid units, and so far the same 0.05 bounded both the solid velocity and the pore fluid velocity. In the tutorial a fluid limit 3 times looser changes the radial temperatures by at most 3 K. This PR gives the fluid its own key, `time.dxymax_fluid`, with a default of 0.15. The solid limit stays at 0.05. A looser fluid step also loosens the explicit upwind fluid heat term of the thermal solve, whose bound (the inflow sum per node at or below 1) no limit checked. The PR adds that limit: dt is at most the inverse of the largest inflow rate over the nodes. ## Changes - Config (`src/config.jl`): `TimeConfig.dxymax_fluid`, default 0.15, validated in (0, 1] and finite like `dxymax`. - Time step (`src/numerics/timestep.jl`): the vxf and vyf lines of `compute_displacement_timestep` use `dxymax_fluid_val`; `compute_adaptive_timestep` passes it on and takes `fluid_heat_rate`, which limits dt to `1 / fluid_heat_rate` when it is positive. - Fluid heat limit (`src/numerics/thermal.jl`): `fluid_advection_inflow_rate` returns the largest sum over inflow faces of `rhocpf(T_up) |q| / (RHOCP h)`, with the same face rate helper as `compute_fluid_advection_heat!`; a NaN flux or a non-finite heat capacity raises `DomainError`. - Step wiring (`src/simulation/steps/solve_stokes_darcy.jl`, `solve_thermal_energy.jl`): the post-processing step computes the rate from the Darcy fluxes that set the step and passes both values;

prs.title: Remove the net body force of the enclosed mass gravity
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview The default gravity mode, `:enclosed_mass`, builds a radial field about a fixed centre from the mass inside each radius. That field keeps only the monopole part of the mass distribution, that is, the part that depends on radius alone. When the density is not radially symmetric, for example when a dense region is on one side of the body, the sum of rho g over the grid is not zero. Self gravity cannot push an isolated body. This net force is therefore a defect of the model. On main it moves the whole planetesimal through the domain. In the lunar growth tutorial (Nx=33, run to 0.45 Myr) the original rock markers drift about 26 km from the fixed centre on main. The body radius is about 74 km, so this is a large part of the body. After each `:enclosed_mass` gravity solve I now subtract one uniform acceleration, chosen so that the net body force in the 2-D momentum balance is zero. The potential gets the matching linear term, so g = -grad(FI) still holds. The drift in the tutorial drops below 0.1 km. The `:poisson2d` mode is unchanged. ## Changes - Gravity (`src/numerics/gravity.jl`, 64 lines): new `remove_net_body_acceleration!(gx, gy, FI, RHOX, RHOY, coords; xcenter, ycenter)`. It computes a_x = sum(RHOX gx) / sum(RHOX) over the Vx nodes that have a momentum equation. It computes a_y in the same way over the Vy nodes. It then subtracts a from gx and gy and adds a_x (x - xc) + a_y (y - yc) to FI. A component with zero summed density is left unchanged. The function chec

prs.title: Move pore fluid heat transport into the thermal solve
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Summary Rock markers in the lunar growth tutorial reach temperatures far above every grid node: 2909 K against a grid maximum of 1518 K at step 1500. These temperatures come from the pore fluid heat correction in `move_markers_rk4!`. This PR removes that correction and adds pore fluid heat transport to the thermal solve, as a first-order upwind term on the grid. The tutorial now has no marker more than 50 K above the grid maximum on both meshes I ran. At `Nx = 33`, its grid temperature profile moves by at most 6 K at about 0.40 Myr. ## Physics impact On `main`, each marker changes temperature in the advection step. The change is the difference between `tk2` at the marker position before the move and `tk2` at a point reached by moving with the solid velocity and then back along the fluid velocity. The weight of this change is the fluid share of the marker heat capacity, so it depends on the porosity of the marker. A heat budget of the hottest marker in the tutorial at step 1500 gives +2123 K from this correction and -14 K from the thermal update. I did not find why the correction accumulates on some markers. Turning the correction off gives 0 hot markers in the same run. On this branch, markers keep their temperature during advection. Each interior pressure node gets a heat source from the faces with inflow, `rhocp_f(T_up) * |q| * (T_up - T) / h`. This is the upwind form of `-rhocp_f q . grad(T)` in the frame of the solid. Markers take this heat through the normal grid to m

prs.title: Treat the 2-D section as a sphere by default
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Summary A planetesimal is a sphere, but the default run treated its 2-D section as a disk: heat left through a surface that grew as r and gravity followed a cylinder. The defaults now treat the section as a slice through a sphere. `geometry.spherical_metric` is `true`, so conduction has the radial term of a sphere and inventories weight each marker by its out-of-plane length 2r. `geometry.gravity_mode` is `enclosed_mass`, so gravity follows the mass inside each shell. Flow stays 2-D. Enclosed mass gravity is also now the discrete gradient of a potential on the grid. The radial vector that the mode evaluated at velocity nodes had a discrete curl, and this curl drove a false circulation in a body at rest. ## Physics impact Before and after values, 100 steps, one thread, config as shipped, `main` at 8ee40a5a0c9e707b464f2e5aa88fb93db7622e08 against this branch: | Config | Output | `main` | This branch | |---|---|---|---| | `core_formation_benchmark` | Coldest rock marker | 379.29 K | 400.87 K | | `core_formation_benchmark` | Mean rock marker temperature | 1237.56 K | 1245.24 K | | `magma_ocean_cooling_turb_on_32` | Model time reached | 6.459 yr | 6.226 yr | | `magma_ocean_cooling_turb_on_32` | Mean rock marker temperature | 1787.16 K | 1787.09 K | | `default` | Mean rock marker temperature | 277.15 K | 276.10 K | The reference diagnostic of `core_formation_benchmark` at 3 steps changes more: the plain 2-D sum of grid density rises from 2.4212e13 to 2.6425e13 (+9.14 %) and the

prs.title: Stop cold markers from cooling further below their nodes
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Summary A cold rock marker could cool without limit and stop a run with a negative temperature. A marker that is colder than all 4 of its nodes now keeps its temperature when the grid increment is negative, and the rejected cooling goes to the other rock markers at the same nodes. ## Physics impact A marker gets only the temperature change of its nodes. When flow carries hot rock past a node, the next projection warms that node, while a cold marker in the cell still takes the node's conductive cooling at each step. I measured this at one node of the lunar growth run with `spherical_metric=true` and `gravity_mode="enclosed_mass"`, on the branch that makes these 2 settings the default: the solve lowers it by 3 K to 5 K per step, marker advection raises it by 4 K to 6 K, the marker falls by 0.9 K to 1.7 K per step, and it never rejoins the grid. With frozen marker positions in the same run, the coldest marker stays near 97 K through 300 steps, and without frozen positions the run stops at 0.22 Myr. Before and after values, `lunar_growth_tutorial`, 400 steps, one thread. Each row compares `main` with this branch: | Setting | Output | `main` | This branch | |---|---|---|---| | Config as shipped | Coldest rock marker | 63.96 K | 139.54 K | | Config as shipped | Mean rock marker temperature | 850.56 K at 0.4335 Myr | 847.33 K at 0.4344 Myr | | Config as shipped | Hottest rock marker | 1484.4 K | 1555.1 K | | Config as shipped | Radius | 73.936 km | 73.988 km | | `spherical_metric

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: This release adds the sub-grid surface lid, the solid rheology and a prescribed surface temperature, and it changes several defaults, so runs give other results than with 26.10.22. Changes to results and defaults: - `matprop_smooth_width` defaults to 0.01, and invalid widths are refused (#88). - The NumPy path computes the thermal expansivity from the thermodynamic identity (#90). - The phase-boundary rate cap is relaxed below the solidus (#92). - The core heat of a call is booked from its integrated temperature change (#106). - A cell entropy outside the EOS tables is refused with the rheology off (#98). New: - A sub-grid conductive lid for a crust thinner than the top cell (#100), under a fixed surface temperature, and under the surface of an atmosphere with its base at the solidus (#108). All lid settings are off by default. - The solid rheology in the entropy solver (#89, #85), a prescribed surface temperature (outer boundary 5, #86), surface and CMB mesh refinement (#93), the liquidus of an iron core alloy with S, C and O (#105), and a check of a P-S table set against published values (#99). The docs have a Validation tab with plots, written for students.

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: This release changes the default IW buffer and two equilibrium constants, so outgassing results differ from 26.10.05. Changes to results and defaults: - The Hirschmann (2021) IW buffer is the default (#39). The Fischer buffer stays available as `fischer`. - The H2S and NH3 equilibrium constants are refit on JANAF data (#40). New: - A metal reservoir that partitions H, C, N and S into the core at one moment of a run (#43). - `calliope.core_split.split_core_mantle`, which splits the bulk H, C, N and S between core and mantle with partition laws from the literature, with a registry for user laws (#47). PROTEUS does not call it yet. - Cross-code consistency tests against atmodeller (#41). The docs have rewritten Validation pages with plots, an explanation and a tutorial for the core split, and a how-to for adding a partition law.

facts.new: Conductive skin thickness [m], or 'saturation' (together with `surface_k`) to use the total thickness of the saturated condensate layers, such as graphite, that float on the surface. 'saturation' needs `surf_state='skin'`; while the layers are negligible the surface is fixed (T_surf = T_magma).

facts.old: Conductive skin thermal conductivity [W m-1 K-1].
facts.new: Conductive skin thermal conductivity [W m-1 K-1], or 'saturation' to combine the conductivities of the stacked condensate layers in series, k = d / sum(d_i / k_i).

entries.title: CALLIOPE default IW buffer and refit equilibrium constants
entries.text: CALLIOPE now uses the Hirschmann IW buffer by default instead of the Fischer buffer, and the H2S and NH3 equilibrium constants are refit. Outgassing results differ from the previous release. PROTEUS tests now follow the buffer, for example the all-dummy run ends with a different status and the low-H cold start has a different surface pressure.

entries.title: Aragog 26.11.08 changes defaults and numerics
entries.text: The new Aragog release changes the default smoothing width of material properties, computes the thermal expansivity on the NumPy path from the thermodynamic identity, relaxes the phase-boundary rate cap below the solidus and books the core heat of a call from its integrated temperature change. Runs give other results than with the previous release.

entries.title: One density source for the dummy and boundary interiors
entries.text: The duplicate density settings of the dummy and boundary interiors are deprecated and ignored. The dummy interior now reports its mantle mass over the mantle shell volume as its density, and the boundary interior takes its masses and core radius from the structure. Configs that set these densities now get the structure values.

entries.title: Surface skin from saturated condensates
entries.text: A new option builds the conductive skin between magma and atmosphere from condensates that atmodeller saturates at the surface, such as graphite, stacked as layers in series. The structure plot now joins interior and atmosphere profiles, and SPIDER profile plots now cover the full run. A new output column holds the conductivity of the boundary layer.

entries.title: Sub-grid crust lid in Aragog and an iron alloy liquidus
entries.text: Aragog can now carry a crust thinner than its top cell as a sub-grid lid, under a fixed surface temperature or under the surface of an atmosphere with its base at the solidus. The lid is off by default. Aragog also gains the liquidus of an iron core alloy with S, C and O.

entries.title: Core and mantle split of H, C, N and S in CALLIOPE
entries.text: CALLIOPE can now split the bulk H, C, N and S of a planet between the metal core and the silicate mantle with partition laws from the literature, and users can register their own laws. PROTEUS does not call this yet.

entries.title: Escape regime dispatcher in ZEPHYRUS
entries.text: ZEPHYRUS can now classify a planetary state into one of six escape regimes and return one bulk mass-loss rate, split over species by a fractionation closure. It is a standalone interface for now, and the PROTEUS coupling follows later.

entries.title: Calibrated core alloy density in Zalmoxis
entries.text: The light-element density law of the core alloy in Zalmoxis is now calibrated on the outer cores of Hirose et al. for S, Si, O and H. The two hydrogen laws have new names, and the old linear hydrogen name is refused with an error that names the replacements.

entries.title: Option to load only the gases that PROTEUS models in AGNI
entries.text: A new AGNI option loads opacities only for the gases that PROTEUS models, with the previous behaviour kept as the default. The AGNI pin moves to a newer version that fetches different basic spectral files.

entries.title: install.sh no longer installs Julia
entries.text: The installer now uses a Julia 1.13 that it finds and stops with the commands to run when it finds none, before it creates an environment. The install page has a new step for Julia. Existing installs are not affected.

entries.title: JANUS fix for long output paths
entries.text: PROTEUS now requires the JANUS release that stops InsertStellarSpectrum from hanging and filling the disk on a long output path. Such a run now stops at the first atmosphere call with a clear error. Spectral files are unchanged on normal input.

entries.title: 40 new SOCRATES spectral files
entries.text: PROTEUS can now fetch 40 new SOCRATES spectral files, in several families and band counts, from Zenodo with DataverseNL mirrors. A bare spectral download is now about 7.5 GB. This needs the new fwl-io floor.

entries.title: Erebus treats the 2-D section as a sphere by default
entries.text: The default Erebus run now uses spherical conduction and enclosed mass gravity, and the net body force of that gravity is removed so the body no longer drifts. Pore fluid heat moves into the thermal solve, the pore fluid has its own displacement limit, and cold markers no longer cool without limit.

entries.title: Zalmoxis logging and output folder
entries.text: Zalmoxis loggers now sit under the fwl name, so PROTEUS captures their messages, and per-iteration messages moved to debug level. A standalone run writes all its files into one output folder, and the debug profile dump is written only into a folder that the caller names.

entries.title: New SciPy dependency in ZEPHYRUS
entries.text: The escape dispatcher adds SciPy as a dependency of ZEPHYRUS.

entries.title: Aragog lid coupled to the atmosphere surface
entries.text: This pull request couples the Aragog sub-grid lid to the surface balance of PROTEUS as an off-by-default option. The atmosphere sees the lid and the open surface as two conductors in parallel, and the energy that the lid stores or releases is booked.

entries.title: Separate Julia depot for each PROTEUS install
entries.text: This pull request gives each install its own Julia package folder, so that two installs on one machine no longer share packages. It is not meant to change run results.
